changes.title: The inventory print graded the triangle: builds everywhere, and Brent rose anyway
changes.vintage: EIA report for the week ending Nov 6, released Nov 12
changes.delta: Crude +4.657 million barrels against a survey draw; Brent settled +3.3 percent on the same day
changes.body: The report printed crude up 4.657 million barrels to 414.4 million, gasoline up 1.8 million, distillate up 4.1 million to 103.3 million and total commercial petroleum up 11.4 million, against a Reuters poll draw of 1.1 million and a Wall Street Journal survey draw of 0.7 million. Brent Jan27 settled at $95.82, up about $3.06, and the Brent to WTI spread widened to $7.08. The distillate build is the first loosening against stocks that stood at their lowest since May 2003; the level remains 8 percent below the five-year average.
changes.balance: A US system that builds at 95.2 percent runs is not short of crude this week; the Canadian balance still tanks about 200 kb/d a month toward 76.24 million barrels in December against 80.6 million of working capacity.
changes.conditional: A second straight build week would remove the one-week-noise defence; a return to draws restores the tight reading.

changes.title: The differential widening moved into the deferred strip
changes.delta: December zero lots for a sixth session; deferred tenors widened on 345 to 480 lots each
changes.body: December WCS is -$28.36 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 12) on zero lots, a sixth straight session without a trade. January is -$25.20, wider by $0.35 on 2 lots. April through November widened on 345 to 480 lots a tenor. Houston followed the same shape, January -$17.75 on 2 lots with the deferred strip wider on volume. The December ARV to TMW spread is +$9.19 and January's is +$7.45. December WCS outright is $60.38.
changes.balance: The front month's missing fact is still a trade; the deferred volume says length is expressing itself where length sits, ahead of the Nov 17 nominations close.
changes.conditional: December's first trade at a wider level confirms the deferred signal at the front; a tighter first trade breaks it.

changes.title: Abu Dhabi's prisoner numbers missed their due date
changes.delta: No final number confirmed; the round has no landed deliverable and the energy truce is unanswered
changes.body: The prisoner exchange remains agreed in principle only, with ranges of 1,000 to 1,500 a side and no confirmed final figure as of Nov 13, against a Nov 12 due date. There is no ceasefire, no territory agreement and no answer to Kyiv's sea and energy truce offer. The US mediators travelled to Moscow on Nov 12 with no outcome established. In the Gulf, the President posted that the United States does not need a deal with Iran, and the UKMTO-confirmed incident is the Dominica Prosperity off Ras Al-Khaimah on Nov 11.
changes.balance: No diplomatic item in the window changes a November barrel; Gulf exports remain set by transit, bypass and escort capacity.
changes.conditional: A confirmed prisoner figure lands the round's first deliverable; an answer on the truce, either way, is its first energy content.

calendar.title: Possible producer and government announcement on pipelines, production growth and GHG abatement (soft target, falls on a Sunday)
calendar.impact: The date is unconfirmed and unslipped. Alberta's Pacific Link royalty incentives are the provincial leg of the same file. No terms are announced and no volumes are committed.

calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close
calendar.impact: The deadline for December shipper nominations. The registered December call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows, with December still without a trade after six sessions.

calendar.title: Irving Saint John Operation Osprey resumption date
calendar.impact: The last dated outage in the window is scheduled to resume operations on Nov 18, with no completion release yet.

calendar.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework
calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework. The November monthly report leaves demand growth unchanged and prints October production at 41.23 million barrels a day on secondary sources.

flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, nominations close Nov 17
flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The registered December call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack includes the balance build with supply running about 200 kb/d a month above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a December front month that has not traded in six sessions, deferred strip widening on volume, and a Brent to WTI spread at $7.08. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; the Enbridge notice follows and grades the call.
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice, or a material change in the physical backdrop before the close

flags.title: Distillate: one build against a stocks position still 8 percent below its five-year average
flags.body: Distillate stocks rose 4.1 million barrels to 103.3 million in the week ending Nov 6, the first build against a position that stood at 99.3 million, the lowest since May 2003. The validated diesel crack is $92.32. Russian refining capacity is estimated down about 30 percent since late October by industry sources.
flags.trigger: The next weekly distillate print, or a fresh Russian refining assessment

flags.title: The Brent to WTI spread at $7.08 is the export arb's first testable setup in weeks
flags.body: Thursday's $7.08 settle is the widest spread in this sequence and the closest the spread leg has come to the $7.49 level at which the arb was already shut on Nov 5. No reopening is confirmed on any print. Baltic Week 46, with the next freight levels, publishes after the week ending Nov 13.
flags.trigger: A second settle above $7 with the Week 46 freight print, or a relapse below $6.50
